How it was obtained (authorized CTF, service challenge:1337 running /workspace/chall.py):

Target: 5-round SPN, 16 x 6-bit S-boxes (96-bit block), 96-bit key; key schedule rk_{i+1}=S(rotl(rk_i,7)); option 1 gives ECB encryption of chosen hex (50000-block quota); option 2 prints the flag iff the submitted integer equals round_keys[0]. The S-box is printed per connection and the S-box/key are fresh per connection, while the flag is fixed.

Attack (integral / square, implemented in /workspace/exploit.py):
1. Query 64-plaintext structures that vary all 64 values of one 6-bit S-box position, others constant (one query per batch of structures). This is a higher-order integral: empirically, over hundreds of random S-box/key instances, every 6-bit group of state X3 (after 3 rounds) XORs to zero 100% of the time, and every 6-bit group of X4 (the final S-box input) XORs to zero with probability ~0.867 (per-chunk 0.865-0.870; per (varied group, output chunk) cell 0.843-0.892).
2. Since C = S(X4) ^ rk5 chunk-wise, for each of the 16 ciphertext 6-bit chunks and each guess k in 0..63, count structures satisfying XOR_texts SINV(ct_chunk ^ k) == 0. The true rk5 chunk is the argmax (~0.87 of structures) while wrong guesses rarely score; 16-20 structures (= 1024-1280 of 50000 blocks) give wide margins (observed key-chunk margins 3-8; simulated 1000/1000 exact full-key recoveries at 16 structures).
3. Invert the key schedule 5 times: rk_i = rotr(SINV(rk_{i+1}),7) to get rk0 = round_keys[0].
4. Verify locally by re-encrypting every queried plaintext with the recovered key and comparing with the service's ciphertexts; only then submit option 2.
